mean: staring fixedly, not taking one's eyes off

use.how: Usually adverbial before 地看着 / 地盯着: 他目不转睛地看着屏幕。 Said of someone watching something visible with complete attention.

near.diff: 全神贯注 is full concentration on any task, even listening or working; 目不转睛 is only about the eyes staying fixed on something seen.

cue: At the show the children never once looked away from the magician's hands as he slowly made the coin vanish. How were they watching?

ctx.s: 孩子们{目不转睛}地看着魔术师的手。
ctx.en: The children watched the magician's hands without taking their eyes off them.

ctx.s: 小猫蹲在鱼缸边，{目不转睛}地看着里面游来游去的金鱼。
ctx.en: The kitten crouched by the fish tank, eyes fixed on the goldfish swimming back and forth.

ctx.s: “你怎么一直{目不转睛}地盯着那幅画？”“我觉得它好像在对我笑。”
ctx.en: "Why do you keep staring at that painting?" "It feels like it's smiling at me."

ctx.s: 比赛只剩最后一分钟，全场观众都{目不转睛}地盯着球门，谁也不敢眨眼。
ctx.en: With one minute left in the match, the whole crowd kept their eyes glued to the goal, nobody daring to blink.

ctx.s: 他坐在电视机前{目不转睛}，连饭都忘了吃。
ctx.en: He sat in front of the TV staring at the screen, so absorbed he forgot to eat.

ctx.s: 她{目不转睛}地盯着屏幕，连眼睛都不敢眨，生怕错过自己的名字。
ctx.en: She stared at the screen without daring to blink, afraid of missing her own name.

bad.s: 我{目不转睛}地听着老师讲课。
bad.en: (meant: I listened to the teacher with full attention)
bad.why: It describes the eyes fixed on something seen; for listening attentively a different idiom of concentration is needed.

bad.s: 他学习一向{目不转睛}，所以成绩很好。
bad.en: (meant: he always studies with concentration)
bad.why: It is a moment of fixed staring at a particular sight, not a general habit of diligence.

mean: so arrogant that no one else counts
lit: there is nobody in his eyes

use.how: Predicate or attributive, often with 太 or 变得: 他太目中无人了。 Criticises someone who treats others as if they did not matter.

near.diff: 自以为是 is being sure one is always right; 目中无人 is ignoring and slighting other people altogether.

cue: Since winning the award, the new star of the team ignores the coach, interrupts senior players and greets no one. How is he behaving?

ctx.s: 他考了第一名以后就{目中无人}，见了同学也不打招呼。
ctx.en: After coming first in the exam he became arrogant and doesn't even greet his classmates.

ctx.s: 这个新来的经理太{目中无人}了，跟老员工说话总是一副看不起人的样子。
ctx.en: The new manager is far too arrogant; he always talks down to the long-serving staff.

ctx.s: “别那么{目中无人}，人家跟你说话，你至少看人家一眼。”
ctx.en: "Don't be so arrogant; when someone talks to you, at least look at them."

ctx.s: 球队连赢了几场，有些队员开始{目中无人}，结果输给了一支弱队。
ctx.en: After a string of wins some players got cocky, and the team lost to a weak side.

ctx.s: 她说话的态度那么{目中无人}，难怪大家都不愿意跟她合作。
ctx.en: She talks to people with such disdain that it's no wonder nobody wants to work with her.

ctx.s: 一个人再有本事，也不能{目中无人}，把别人都不放在眼里。
ctx.en: However capable you are, you can't act as if no one else matters and look down on everyone.

bad.s: 他工作的时候非常专心，{目中无人}。
bad.en: (meant: he was so focused he didn't notice anyone around him)
bad.why: It means arrogance toward others, not being too absorbed to notice them.

bad.s: 老师夸我做事{目中无人}，我特别高兴。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher praised me for being independent)
bad.why: It is always a criticism; no teacher would use it as praise.

lit: heads come together, mouths reach ears

use.how: Predicate for two or more people physically close, often where they should be quiet: 台下的人开始交头接耳。

near.diff: 窃窃私语 stresses talking secretly in low voices; 交头接耳 pictures people leaning heads together, often in a class, meeting or crowd.

cue: As soon as the manager mentions layoffs, people around the meeting table lean toward their neighbours and start murmuring. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 上课的时候不要{交头接耳}。
ctx.en: Don't whisper to each other during class.

ctx.s: 考试时有两个学生{交头接耳}，被老师警告了。
ctx.en: Two students whispered to each other during the exam and got a warning from the teacher.

ctx.s: “后排两位同学，你们{交头接耳}的，在说什么呢？”老师停下来问。
ctx.en: "You two in the back row, what are you whispering about?" the teacher stopped to ask.

ctx.s: 经理一宣布要裁员，会议室里的人就开始{交头接耳}。
ctx.en: The moment the manager announced layoffs, people in the meeting room started whispering to one another.

ctx.s: 新娘一出场，客人们纷纷{交头接耳}，夸她今天真漂亮。
ctx.en: When the bride appeared, the guests leaned over to each other, whispering how lovely she looked.

ctx.s: 电影院里，前排两个人一直{交头接耳}，影响了旁边的观众。
ctx.en: In the cinema two people in the front row kept whispering, disturbing everyone near them.

bad.s: 他一个人在房间里{交头接耳}。
bad.en: (meant: he was muttering to himself in his room)
bad.why: It needs at least two people leaning together; one person alone cannot do it.

bad.s: 我们俩在电话里{交头接耳}了一个小时。
bad.en: (meant: we chatted quietly on the phone for an hour)
bad.why: The image is heads physically close; it cannot describe a phone call.

lit: the hands dance and the feet stamp

story.text: The Preface to the Book of Songs explains how poetry and dance arise from feeling: what stirs inside comes out as words; when words are not enough, one sighs; when sighing is not enough, one sings; and when singing is not enough, without knowing it the hands begin to dance and the feet to stamp.

use.how: Often after 高兴得 / 乐得, or adverbial with 地: 他高兴得手舞足蹈。 Describes visible, bodily excitement from joy.

near.diff: 欢天喜地 is a general air of great happiness; 手舞足蹈 shows the joy in waving arms and jumping feet.

cue: Your little brother hears you're going to the theme park tomorrow and starts jumping, flapping his arms and spinning round the room. How is he reacting?

ctx.s: 听说明天去游乐园，弟弟高兴得{手舞足蹈}。
ctx.en: Hearing we were going to the theme park tomorrow, my little brother jumped about with joy.

ctx.s: 宝宝听到音乐，在床上{手舞足蹈}，逗得全家人都笑了。
ctx.en: When the baby heard the music she kicked and waved on the bed, making the whole family laugh.

ctx.s: “你看你，{手舞足蹈}的，是不是中奖了？”
ctx.en: "Look at you, bouncing around like that — did you win the lottery?"

ctx.s: 进球了！他在沙发上{手舞足蹈}地大喊大叫。
ctx.en: Goal! He leapt about on the sofa, shouting and waving his arms.

ctx.s: 收到录取通知书那天，她挥着信在厨房里{手舞足蹈}，把妈妈都逗笑了。
ctx.en: The day her acceptance letter came, she waved it about and danced round the kitchen, making her mother laugh.

ctx.s: 他一说起自己喜欢的球队就{手舞足蹈}，兴奋得停不下来。
ctx.en: Whenever he talks about his favourite team he gets so excited his arms and legs never stop moving.

bad.s: 她在舞蹈课上{手舞足蹈}，跳了一支芭蕾。
bad.en: (meant: she danced a ballet in dance class)
bad.why: It is excited, joyful flailing, not actual dancing; for real dancing just use the ordinary verb for dancing.

bad.s: 听说奶奶住院了，他急得{手舞足蹈}。
bad.en: (meant: he was so anxious he couldn't keep still)
bad.why: It expresses joy, not anxiety; for panic or restlessness other idioms are needed.

lit: a straight heart and a quick mouth

use.how: Describes a person's temperament, often as an apology or excuse: 我这个人心直口快，你别介意。 Says what one thinks at once, without malice.

near.diff: 直言不讳 is speaking frankly on a particular serious matter; 心直口快 is a personality that blurts out what it thinks.

cue: Your grandmother always says exactly what she thinks the moment she thinks it — like telling you right away that you've put on weight. What kind of person is she?

ctx.s: 我这个人{心直口快}，说错了你别生气。
ctx.en: I'm the type who says what I think; don't be upset if I say something wrong.

ctx.s: 奶奶是个{心直口快}的人，看见我胖了就直接说出来。
ctx.en: Grandma is very outspoken; she saw I'd put on weight and said so straight away.

ctx.s: “他不是故意的，就是{心直口快}，想到什么说什么。”
ctx.en: "He didn't mean it; he's just blunt and says whatever comes into his head."

ctx.s: 她{心直口快}，有什么意见当场就说出来。
ctx.en: She's frank by nature; if she has an objection she voices it on the spot.

ctx.s: 小王{心直口快}，开会时一句话就点破了方案的问题，经理有点尴尬。
ctx.en: Xiao Wang is outspoken; in the meeting he pointed out the plan's flaw in one sentence, and the manager looked awkward.

ctx.s: 跟{心直口快}的朋友相处，至少不用猜他心里在想什么。
ctx.en: With a blunt friend, at least you never have to guess what he's really thinking.

bad.s: 他说话{心直口快}，一分钟能说两百个字。
bad.en: (meant: he talks very fast)
bad.why: The 'quick mouth' is not speech speed; it means saying what one thinks right away and frankly.

bad.s: 他{心直口快}，嘴上说好，心里却不同意。
bad.en: (meant: he agrees outwardly but disagrees inside)
bad.why: It means mouth and heart match; saying yes while disagreeing is the opposite.

lit: convinced in the heart and conceding with the mouth

use.how: Said by or of the one persuaded or defeated, often after 让…, 输得, 我就: 他讲得有理，我心服口服。

near.diff: 甘拜下风 is a modest admission of losing to a better rival; 心服口服 can also mean being won over by an argument or evidence.

cue: You argued hard that you were right, but your friend calmly showed you the evidence, point by point, and now you have no objection left at all. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 他的解释很有道理，我{心服口服}。
ctx.en: His explanation makes perfect sense; I'm completely convinced.

ctx.s: 这场比赛我们输得{心服口服}，对手确实比我们强。
ctx.en: We lost this match fair and square; our opponents really were better.

ctx.s: “你要是能拿出证据，我就{心服口服}。”
ctx.en: "If you can show me the evidence, I'll admit you're right."

ctx.s: 老师没有批评他，只是把错误一条条讲清楚，让他{心服口服}。
ctx.en: The teacher didn't scold him; she just explained each mistake clearly until he fully accepted it.

ctx.s: 她一个月就把销售额翻了一倍，原来不看好她的人都{心服口服}了。
ctx.en: She doubled sales in a month, and the people who had doubted her were completely won over.

ctx.s: 光靠吓唬是没用的，要让孩子{心服口服}，得跟他讲道理。
ctx.en: Threats don't work; if you want a child to genuinely accept it, you have to reason with him.

bad.s: 老板逼我签字，我只好{心服口服}地签了。
bad.en: (meant: I reluctantly signed because my boss forced me)
bad.why: It means genuine, willing acceptance; giving in under pressure is the opposite.

bad.s: 这次我赢了，所以对结果{心服口服}。
bad.en: (meant: I won, so I'm satisfied with the result)
bad.why: It is said by the side that was persuaded or beaten, not by the winner.

lit: the heart is full and the wishes are satisfied

use.how: Adverbial with 地, or predicate often with 就…了: 有这些我就心满意足了。 A calm, complete contentment, not excitement.

near.diff: 心花怒放 is bursting, elated joy; 心满意足 is quiet contentment with nothing more to wish for.

cue: After a big bowl of hot noodles on a cold night, your father leans back on the sofa, pats his stomach and wants nothing more. How does he feel?

ctx.s: 吃了一大碗热面条，他{心满意足}地躺在沙发上。
ctx.en: After a big bowl of hot noodles he lay back on the sofa, perfectly content.

ctx.s: 小猫吃饱了，{心满意足}地舔着爪子。
ctx.en: Its stomach full, the kitten contentedly licked its paws.

ctx.s: 只要每天能睡到自然醒，我就{心满意足}了。
ctx.en: As long as I can sleep until I wake up naturally every day, I'll be perfectly happy.

ctx.s: 孩子拿到了想要的玩具，再也不吵不闹，{心满意足}地跟着妈妈回家了。
ctx.en: Having got the toy he wanted, the child stopped fussing and went home with his mother, completely satisfied.

ctx.s: “就这么一点工资，你就{心满意足}了？”
ctx.en: "With a salary that small, you're already satisfied?"

ctx.s: 老人看着满屋子的儿孙，脸上露出{心满意足}的笑容。
ctx.en: Looking at the room full of children and grandchildren, the old man smiled with deep contentment.

bad.s: 听到中奖的消息，他{心满意足}地跳了起来。
bad.en: (meant: he leapt up with excitement at winning)
bad.why: It is calm contentment; jumping with excitement calls for an idiom of elation.

bad.s: 这件衣服太{心满意足}了，我马上就买了。
bad.en: (meant: this dress was so satisfying that I bought it at once)
bad.why: It describes how a person feels, not a thing that pleases; a dress cannot be content.

lit: the heart's blood rises like a tide

story.text: In the Ming novel Investiture of the Gods, the immortals have a sign of coming events: when their heart's blood suddenly surges like a rising tide, they know something has happened in the world and work out by divination what it is. In everyday use the phrase came to mean a sudden impulse to do something.

use.how: Predicate or after 一时 / 全凭: 他一时心血来潮，报了个舞蹈班。 For an impulsive decision, often with light mockery.

near.diff: 突发奇想 stresses a strange, original idea popping up; 心血来潮 stresses acting on a sudden impulse, often without thought.

cue: For no reason at all, your flatmate decided at midnight to dye her hair purple, and by morning it was done. Why did she do it?

ctx.s: 他{心血来潮}，半夜跑到楼下去跑步。
ctx.en: On a sudden whim he went downstairs in the middle of the night to go running.

ctx.s: 周末我{心血来潮}，把头发染成了紫色。
ctx.en: At the weekend I had a sudden urge and dyed my hair purple.

ctx.s: “你怎么突然要学钢琴？”“没什么，就是{心血来潮}。”
ctx.en: "Why do you suddenly want to learn the piano?" "No reason, it's just a whim."

ctx.s: 她做事全凭{心血来潮}，今天想开店，明天又想出国。
ctx.en: She does everything on impulse: today she wants to open a shop, tomorrow to move abroad.

ctx.s: 老板一时{心血来潮}改了方案，全组人只好加班重做。
ctx.en: The boss changed the plan on a whim, and the whole team had to work overtime redoing it.

ctx.s: 学外语不能靠一时的{心血来潮}，得每天坚持。
ctx.en: You can't learn a language on a passing impulse; you have to keep at it every day.

bad.s: 经过三个月的认真考虑，他{心血来潮}，决定换工作。
bad.en: (meant: after careful thought he decided to change jobs)
bad.why: It means a sudden, unconsidered impulse; months of careful thought contradict it.

bad.s: 听到这个坏消息，他{心血来潮}，气得说不出话。
bad.en: (meant: his blood boiled with anger)
bad.why: Despite the blood image it has nothing to do with anger; it means a sudden whim.

mean: to have a fair idea of how things stand
lit: there are figures in one's heart

use.how: Predicate, often 对…心中有数 or 做到心中有数: 这件事我心中有数。 Having a clear enough grasp of a situation to handle it.

near.diff: 胸有成竹 is having a ready plan and full confidence of success; 心中有数 is simply knowing roughly where things stand.

cue: Before renovating, you add up the cost of every item so that you know roughly where the money will go and won't be caught out. What have you achieved?

ctx.s: 这件事大概是什么情况，我{心中有数}，你放心吧。
ctx.en: I have a fair idea of how this matter stands; don't worry.

ctx.s: 考试前把重点都复习一遍，就能{心中有数}了。
ctx.en: Go over the key points before the exam and you'll know where you stand.

ctx.s: “预算还剩多少，你{心中有数}吗？”
ctx.en: "Do you have a clear idea of how much budget is left?"

ctx.s: 装修前要把每一项花费都算清楚，做到{心中有数}。
ctx.en: Before renovating, work out every expense so you know exactly where things stand.

ctx.s: 老医生看了片子，{心中有数}，没多说就开了药。
ctx.en: The old doctor looked at the scan, knew what he was dealing with, and wrote a prescription without saying much.

ctx.s: 比赛还剩十分钟，教练看了看比分，对最后怎么打已经{心中有数}。
ctx.en: With ten minutes left, the coach glanced at the score and already had a clear idea of how to play the rest.

bad.s: 他{心中有数}，算术特别好。
bad.en: (meant: he is good at mental arithmetic)
bad.why: The 'figures' here are not maths; it means a clear grasp of a situation.

bad.s: 我对她{心中有数}，想跟她表白。
bad.en: (meant: I have feelings for her)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with affection; it means knowing how matters stand.

mean: to know full well without saying it
lit: the heart knows and the belly is clear

use.how: Predicate, often with 大家 / 都 / 自己: 谁对谁错，大家心知肚明。 For an awkward truth that is understood but left unspoken.

near.diff: 心照不宣 is two sides tacitly agreeing not to mention something; 心知肚明 is simply knowing it full well, even one person alone.

cue: Your friend pretends to have no idea why you're upset with him, but you're sure he knows perfectly well and just won't admit it. What do you tell him?

ctx.s: 谁对谁错，大家都{心知肚明}。
ctx.en: Who was right and who was wrong — everyone knows perfectly well.

ctx.s: “你别装了，为什么生气你自己{心知肚明}。”
ctx.en: "Stop pretending; you know full well why I'm angry."

ctx.s: 他为什么突然请假，我{心知肚明}，只是不想说破。
ctx.en: I know perfectly well why he suddenly took leave; I just don't want to say it.

ctx.s: 这份礼物送得这么贵重，到底是什么意思，她{心知肚明}。
ctx.en: A gift that expensive — she knew perfectly well what it meant.

ctx.s: 价格明显偏高，顾客其实{心知肚明}，只是图个方便。
ctx.en: Customers know full well the prices are too high; they just pay for the convenience.

ctx.s: 经理嘴上说一切正常，其实他自己{心知肚明}，这个项目已经保不住了。
ctx.en: The manager says all is fine, but he knows full well the project can't be saved.

bad.s: 老师讲了两遍，我现在终于{心知肚明}了。
bad.en: (meant: after two explanations I finally understand)
bad.why: It is not about understanding a lesson; it means knowing an unspoken truth full well.

bad.s: 他{心知肚明}地向大家宣布了真相。
bad.en: (meant: he announced the truth to everyone)
bad.why: It is knowing without saying; announcing the truth contradicts it.
